subject.title: fix embedded compaction hook reset API

question: Should after-compaction hooks receive a stable host-owned current-session reset capability across all supported harnesses, including Codex, or should reset authority remain restricted to selected owner-specific runtimes?
rationale: The PR expands the public plugin hook contract and decides which bundled plugin harnesses receive a private session-reset queue; repository policy and upgrade risk require explicit owner intent for that permanent capability boundary.

options.title: Adopt a host-owned cross-harness API
options.body: Approve the capability, replace owner-specific raw-queue handoff with a narrow host bridge, and cover OpenClaw, Copilot, and Codex uniformly.

options.title: Restrict the API to core
options.body: Keep reset authority inside the built-in OpenClaw lifecycle and remove the public or bundled-plugin exposure until a broader contract is designed.

options.title: Pause and split the branch
options.body: Extract the independent tool-loop work and defer the reset API until its plugin and security contract has a dedicated design review.

recommendation.title: Adopt a host-owned cross-harness API
recommendation.body: Approve the capability, replace owner-specific raw-queue handoff with a narrow host bridge, and cover OpenClaw, Copilot, and Codex uniformly.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced and merged the plugin-owned Codex harness architecture and is the strongest available owner for its lifecycle authority boundary.
